summary: Lobsang Dargyay was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery, and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, and later held a post at the University of Vienna from around 1974 to 1980.

Lobsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at Drepung Monastery from circa 1939 to 1959, he served as Head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics in 1985.

Lobsang Jamspal works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tashilhunpo Monastery, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, University of Delhi, and Columbia University.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teachers Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from circa 1990 to 2017, and became Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center around 2018.

Lobsang Tenpa is a scholar in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he studied under Sharad Kumar Soni.

Lobsang Yongdan is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Kumbum Monastery and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He held postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and the University of Bonn.
Loden Sherab Dagyab is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama. He held an academic post at the University of Bonn from circa 1966 to 2004.
Lodrö Sangpo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey around 1993.

Lokesh Chandra is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the University of the Punjab, under Raghu Vira, and at Utrecht University. Around 1963, he became Director of the International Academy of Indian Culture.
Longlian was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun from 1939 to 1940 and under Nenghai from around 1941 to 1967.

Lopon Tenzin Namdak was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Sangye Tenzin, Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and Sherab Tenzin Gyaltsen, and at Menri Monastery. He held posts at Menri Monastery and Triten Norbutse Monastery, co-founding both institutions.

Lore Sander was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. She held posts at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst, Humboldt University, Ludwig Maximilian University, and the Free University of Berlin.

Lori Meeks is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Jacqueline I. Stone, Ryuichi Abe, Masayuki Taira, Yoshiko Oka, and Shunsho Manabe, later holding posts at Stanford University and the University of Southern California.

Lorna Dewaraja was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She held academic posts at St Anne's College and at the University of Ceylon, where she served as Associate Professor of History.
Lorne Ladner is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Thubten Zopa Rinpoche. He served as an adjunct faculty member in the counseling program at Argosy University.

Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Princeton and Harvard, and later held academic posts at the University of Cambridge and as a professor at Heidelberg University.

Lothar von Falkenhausen is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1993 and was a visiting professor at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature in 2003.

Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss, at Collège d'Harcourt, Institut d'ethnologie, EPHE, and EHESS. He held posts at the Musée national des Arts et Traditions Populaires, Oxford, EPHE, and EHESS.

Louis Finot was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. After studying at the École des chartes, he served as the first director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient and as professeur honoraire at the Collège de France.
